Without answer choices, what is the best architecture response to this scenario? A refund tool can transfer money. The system prompt says “never refund more than $500,” but the API accepts any amount. What is the strongest improvement?
Enforce the limit in deterministic transaction/authorization logic before execution. Hard financial limits belong at the execution boundary.
Resolve this production scenario for guardrails and safety controls: A required authorization service is unavailable during a high-risk transaction. What is usually safest?
Block or defer the action until authorization can be verified. High-risk controls commonly fail closed.
What should an architect recommend in this guardrails and safety controls situation? An agent reads untrusted web content and can also modify production systems. Which safety posture is strongest?
Layer prompt-injection defenses with scoped tools, sandboxing/permissions, authorization, and approval where needed. No single prompt-level defense is sufficient.
State the preferred architecture action for this design-review scenario: An output moderation check runs only after an irreversible transfer has already executed. What is wrong?
The control is placed after the point where it could prevent the harmful action. Controls must sit at boundaries where they can enforce the property.
